standard: course-sentence-translation 技能 R1–R4；键取自对齐原串

entries.en: ‘How do you get to school?’
entries.zh: “你怎么去上学？”

entries.en: This question often gets an answer like ‘By bus’ or ‘I walk’ or ‘My parents take me by car’.
entries.zh: 这个问题常常会得到这样的回答：“坐公交车”“我走路”或者“我父母开车送我”。

entries.en: But not always – there are children in many different parts of the world who, every day, have to go on a difficult journey in order to get to their lessons.
entries.zh: 但情况并不总是这样——世界许多地方的孩子每天都要走上一段艰难的路程才能去上课。

entries.en: They travel for kilometres on foot, or by boat, bicycle, donkey or train.
entries.zh: 他们要步行数公里，或者乘船、骑自行车、骑驴或坐火车。

entries.en: They cross deserts, mountains, rivers, snow and ice: for example, the children of the Iñupiat community in Alaska go to school and then come back when it is dark, in extremely cold temperatures.
entries.zh: 他们穿越沙漠、高山、河流、冰雪：例如，阿拉斯加伊努皮亚特社区的孩子们上学，天黑后才回来，气温极低。

entries.en: And they are not the only ones.
entries.zh: 他们并不是唯一这样的孩子。

entries.en: Kids in many countries do this and more.
entries.zh: 许多国家的孩子都是这样，甚至还要面对更多。

entries.en: These children in Indonesia have to cross a bridge ten metres above a dangerous river to get to their class on time.
entries.zh: 印度尼西亚的这些孩子要穿过一座高出危险河流十米的桥，才能准时上课。

entries.en: (Some years ago the bridge fell down after very heavy rain.)
entries.zh: （几年前，这座桥在大雨过后塌了。）

entries.en: Then they walk many more kilometres through the forest to their school in Banten.
entries.zh: 然后他们还要再走很多公里，穿过森林，去万丹的学校。

entries.en: A pupil at Gulu Village Primary School, China, rides a donkey as his grandfather walks beside him.
entries.zh: 中国古卢村小学的一名学生骑着驴，他的祖父走在旁边。

entries.en: Gulu is a mountain village in a national park.
entries.zh: 古卢是国家公园里的一个山村。

entries.en: The school is far away from the village.
entries.zh: 学校离村子很远。

entries.en: It is halfway up a mountain, so it takes five hours to climb from the bottom of the mountain to the school.
entries.zh: 学校在半山腰，所以从山脚爬到学校要花五个小时。

entries.en: The children have a dangerous journey: the path is only 45 centimetres wide in some places.
entries.zh: 孩子们的路程很危险：有些地方的小路只有 45 厘米宽。

entries.en: In Sri Lanka, some children have to cross a piece of wood between two walls of an old castle every morning.
entries.zh: 在斯里兰卡，有些孩子每天早上要走过一块架在古堡两墙之间的木板。

entries.en: Their teacher watches them carefully.
entries.zh: 他们的老师会仔细看着他们。

entries.en: But in Galle, Sri Lanka, many girls don’t go to school – they have to go to work or get married young.
entries.zh: 但在斯里兰卡的加勒，许多女孩不去上学——她们不得不早早工作或结婚。

entries.en: So girls are happy to take a risk in order to get to school.
entries.zh: 因此，为了上学，女孩们愿意冒险。

entries.en: Six-year-old Fabricio Oliveira gets on his donkey every morning to ride with his friends for over an hour through a desert region in the very dry Sertão area of northeast Brazil.
entries.zh: 六岁的法布里西奥·奥利韦拉每天早上骑上驴，和朋友们一起穿越巴西东北部干旱的塞尔陶地区，骑一个多小时。

entries.en: Their school is in Extrema.
entries.zh: 他们的学校在埃克斯特雷马。

entries.en: It’s a tiny village – very few people live there.
entries.zh: 那是一个很小的村庄——那里几乎没人居住。

entries.en: These children live in houses on Chetla Road in Delhi, India.
entries.zh: 这些孩子住在印度德里切特拉路的房子里。

entries.en: Their homes are near the busy and dangerous railway lines that go to Alipur station.
entries.zh: 他们的家靠近通往阿利普尔车站的繁忙而危险的铁路线。

entries.en: Every morning they walk along the tracks to get to their school, 40 minutes away.
entries.zh: 每天早上，他们沿着铁轨走到 40 分钟路程外的学校。

entries.en: So one question we can ask is: why do the children do this?
entries.zh: 所以我们可以问一个问题：孩子们为什么要这样做？

entries.en: Because their parents make them do it?
entries.zh: 是因为父母逼他们这样做吗？

entries.en: The answer, in many cases, is no – it’s because for them going to school means a better future: they hope to get a job and money so they can help their families and their neighbours.
entries.zh: 在很多情况下，答案并不是这样——因为对他们来说，上学意味着更好的未来：他们希望找到工作、挣到钱，帮助家人和邻居。

entries.en: And this is why rivers, deserts or danger won’t stop them on their way to school.
entries.zh: 这就是为什么河流、沙漠或危险都挡不住他们上学的路。
